problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ be bases of ${R}^{2}.$ 
Find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B$ given that

$$
[{c}_{1}]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,[{c}_{2}]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $C$ relative to the basis $B.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
{P}_{C\to B}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$
